headline: Nevro deal fuels sharp growth, profit cools sequentially
summary_short: Q1 revenue rose to $759.9M, up 27.0% y/y but down 8.1% q/q; diluted EPS of $0.90 climbed 66.7% y/y but fell 12.6% q/q, with the Nevro merger contributing $82.7M of the quarter's revenue.
summary_long: Revenue was $759.9M (+27.0% y/y, -8.1% q/q); the Nevro merger, closed April 2025, contributed $82.7M and drove most of the U.S. growth alongside higher spine implantable and neuromonitoring sales. Cost of sales rose 19.8% y/y on Nevro-related costs and freight; gross margin held near 69.2%. SG&A rose 22.6% y/y, mostly Nevro integration spend. Operating income was $150.4M (+55.0% y/y); diluted EPS $0.90 (+66.7% y/y, -12.6% q/q). Effective tax rate fell to 20.9% from 27.2% on integration benefits. Cash rose to $561.0M; capex was $39.6M; no share repurchases this quarter. No forward guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: U.S. sales +25.0% ($121.0M), driven by Nevro sales of $67.2M plus Musculoskeletal Solutions growth of $53.7M (spine implantables +$38.9M, neuromonitoring +$10.1M). International sales +35.6% ($40.7M), also led by Musculoskeletal Solutions and Nevro.
The $38.7M (+19.8%) increase was primarily driven by Nevro product cost of sales ($26.2M), higher volume-driven product cost ($4.0M), and higher freight cost ($4.0M).

SG&A rose $55.0M (+22.6%), primarily $46.1M of Nevro expenses plus higher employee-related costs, partly offset by lower taxes/fees; acquisition-related costs also rose $5.3M on business-acquisition-liability fair-value changes.
Net income growth plus a lower effective tax rate (20.9% vs 27.2% a year ago), which the filing attributes to integration benefits, lifted EPS well above the revenue growth rate.

The quarter's growth is substantially inorganic: Nevro (acquired April 2025) is now consolidated for a full quarter and accounted for $82.7M of the $161.7M y/y revenue increase, with the remainder from organic Musculoskeletal Solutions gains.
